Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 56
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: Oceania
  relationship_status: Divorced
  occupation: Detective
  trauma_type: Physical abuse by caregiver (childhood)
  pcl5: 62

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Olfactory Danger Cue: Burnt smell, Victim Similarity: People who look similar to the victims, Positive Emotion Confusion: Positive emotions
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Similar Clothes: avoid wearing similar clothes, Memory Detachment: I detach myself from the memories, Avoid People: avoid other people
  Threat: Physical Reactivity: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience, Sleep Vigilance: I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert, Hypervigilance: Being superalert or watchful or on guard
  Memory: Cannot Explain Clearly: When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish, Rage on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense rage, Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
  Negative Appraisals: Shattered Beliefs: My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed, Bad Coper: My reactions since the event show that I am a lousy coper, Character Blame: The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am

Vignette:
Thomas, a 56-year-old male of Oceania ethnicity and divorced status, has spent most of his life in law enforcement, working as a detective. His career is marked by a relentless pursuit of justice and truth, a calling that he believed was meant for him from a young age. However, the very profession that has given Thomas purpose also brings with it daily reminders of the trauma that haunts him—a childhood marred by physical abuse at the hands of his caregiver. Thomas's journey to this point began in a small town where he grew up under the shadow of violence and fear. The abusive environment left indelible scars, both emotional and psychological. As an adult, Thomas’s life has been punctuated by triggers that remind him of those dark days. One particular trigger is the burnt smell, which transports him back to moments when his caregiver would light a cigarette after episodes of violence. This olfactory cue often leaves Thomas feeling on edge, physically reacting with an increased heart rate and sweating profusely. Another potent trigger is encountering people who resemble the victims he has seen in his line of work. These resemblances evoke memories that are so vivid and painful that they leave him detached from reality for a moment, forcing him to retreat into himself. He detaches from these memories as a defense mechanism but finds it difficult to explain what happened when asked directly, losing track of the narrative mid-conversation. Thomas has developed several maladaptive strategies over the years to cope with his trauma. He avoids wearing clothes similar to those he wore during abusive incidents and tends to avoid social interactions altogether, fearing that others might see through his façade. The isolation he imposes on himself is a coping mechanism that has led to strained relationships and a sense of loneliness. The hypervigilance that Thomas experiences in his daily life is particularly acute at work. He remains superalert and watchful, constantly scanning for potential threats or reminders of his traumatic past. This state of heightened alertness often interferes with his ability to sleep, as he needs to stay awake and vigilant, perpetuating a cycle of sleep deprivation. The memories of his childhood abuse are fragmented and intrusive. They can be triggered without warning by something in his surroundings, flooding him with intense rage that he struggles to control. Thomas has come to believe that his reactions since the event show that he is a lousy coper, further eroding his self-esteem and confidence in himself. Thomas’s worldview has been irrevocably altered by these experiences. He feels that his beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed, leaving him with a sense of shattered innocence and trust. The trauma has led him to blame himself for what happened, believing that he was somehow responsible due to who he is as a person. Thomas’s current state reflects years of accumulated stress and unresolved trauma. His hypervigilance and avoidance behaviors have taken a toll on his professional life, making it difficult to maintain relationships with colleagues and affecting his performance on the job. The cumulative impact has finally pushed him to seek help, driven by a deep-seated fear that he will continue down this destructive path if left unchecked. What brings Thomas to therapy is not just the desire to alleviate his symptoms but also the hope of reclaiming some semblance of control over his life and finding ways to heal from the wounds of his past. He is cautiously optimistic about the possibility of learning healthier coping mechanisms and rebuilding a more stable sense of self, free from the constant shadow of his traumatic memories.
